rows.24:1190:
Holding it in is bad for your body, whoever you are.
So during the few hours you spend at school, you're bound to go to the restroom a few times.{p}
rows.24:1208:
{f:You always go too|That's just normal}, {f:don't you|isn't it}?
Everyone relies on the school restrooms.
But as far as I know, there was just one person who never used the school restrooms.
It wasn't that he was constipated, or had some strange illness.
No matter what happened, he never, ever went to the toilet.
In other words, he didn't excrete.
Can you believe a person like that exists?
Well, there is one.
His name was Kiyoshi Takeuchi.
He was a third-year when I was a first-year, so he was two years older than me.
So, when you hear about someone who's never once gone to the toilet, don't you picture some huge fatso?
But no, he was skin and bones.
Like a piece of wire.{p}
rows.24:1710: But still, you can't believe there's a person who never excretes, can you?
rows.24:178c:
Right?
I think you're right.
In the end, nobody really believed it either, whatever they said.
Deep down, everyone thought he must be sneaking off to the toilet when no one was looking.
Or else that maybe he was just someone who needed to go abnormally rarely.
As for me, honestly, I just thought Takeuchi was pretty amazing, and I wasn't interested in him beyond that.
I never really wished I didn't have to go to the toilet, or even thought about it.
If anything, I liked that unique feeling of release you get in the toilet.
Maybe I just lack delicacy?
So I knew about Takeuchi, but it was all one-sided; he didn't even know I existed.
There was no way our paths would ever cross.
But then.
One day, believe it or not, Takeuchi came up and talked to me.
I was totally shocked.{p}
rows.24:2940:
"Hosoda, are you free today?"
He asked me that out of the blue.
I was thrown.
While I was fumbling for words,
"If you're free, why don't you come over to my place?"
he even asked.
Why would Takeuchi invite me to his house? The mystery only got deeper.
No matter how I thought about it, I couldn't find a reason.
Why me?
Why would he need to invite someone like me to his home?
Maybe there was no need to think so hard about it, but that's just how I am.
I can't help thinking about things.
I didn't know how to answer him.{p}Takeuchi seemed to be waiting for my answer...
rows.24:2ee0:
The inside was amazing too.
Maybe that's what hotels abroad are like?
Well, I've never seen one, so I wouldn't know.
"Make yourself at home.
You don't have to tiptoe around me.
Don't hold back, okay?"
He said it with a laugh, but... easier said than done.
We lived in completely different worlds.
Everything I saw and touched was new to me.{p}
rows.24:38a4:
Then he jerked his chin toward the Sanbura tea.
No toilet in the house?
Can you believe that?
What's more, he was saying it wasn't just Takeuchi who never went; it was everyone in the house.
I was so shocked I couldn't speak.
"That tea is really good for your health.
It removes all the impurities from your body.
It turns what would normally become waste into sweat, and pushes it out through every pore of your body.
So no matter how much you eat, you never get fat.
And it's good for you, too.
Isn't that wonderful?"
That's what he started saying.
What would you do?{p}Should I try drinking the tea?
rows.24:3b04:
Takeuchi edged closer to me.
His face was still smiling, but there was something really frightening about him.
"Come on, there's no need to be shy.
Drink that tea and right away you won't need to go to the toilet anymore.
And it changes your body's whole constitution. It's amazing.
It feels fantastic.
Come on, just humor me and drink it."{p}
rows.24:540c:
Actually, I tried it myself.
Not going to the toilet at school, I mean.
But I couldn't do it.
Sure, for two or three days I can tough it out somehow.
But you have to keep it up until the people around you notice.
There's no way I could keep it up that long.
I was really impressed by how amazing Takeuchi was.
And then I discovered that Takeuchi had an interesting hobby.{p}
rows.24:80c0:
Maybe that's what saved me.
Even now, my body is still normal.
If I hadn't thrown up back then, I wonder if my body would have turned out like his by now.
Rumor had it that Takeuchi never went to the toilet, and of course he didn't.
He's a plant, after all.
You guys are the first people I've ever told this story to.
I haven't turned into anything like that.
That's why I told you all this story.
If I had turned into that, there's no way I'd tell a story like this.
It's true.
I'm a normal human being...
{a}{f:|}, you believe me, right? Right?
..............................
..............................
That's the end of what happened to me.
I wonder who's next.{p}
rows.24:968c:
A plant.
No, can I even call it a plant?
The toilets in the old school building are the old pit kind, right?
A big plant with a man's face was growing out of the toilet.
The thing was green all over, with red mottled spots here and there.
Its main body had lots of horizontal wrinkles, and it looked soft and flabby.
Its roots stuck out over the edge of the toilet.
There were two thick roots, with lots of thin roots growing off them.
And they were shaped like human legs.
And below its face grew branches shaped like arms.
And that plant...
had the very same face as Takeuchi.
Was Takeuchi raising that plant in the toilet?
Was this his secret?
The plant with Takeuchi's face slithered back down into the toilet with a rustling hiss.
Its movements were so very supple.{p}
rows.24:9a60:
I ran along the edge of the back courtyard, and when I got near the new school building, I could see a few students heading home.
Now that I'd come this far, I'd be safe.
...And that's when it happened.
Now that I'd relaxed, I suddenly needed to go to the toilet.{p}What do you think I did?
